subject: Re: StreamCart - request for incident remedy (ex-gratia/top-up authorization)

From: Asha Menon <asha@streamcart.com>

Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency/regression - request for remediation

Marcus —

Thanks for hopping on the call earlier. To summarize: between 2027-03-27 15:40 and 2027-03-27 17:50 PDT we experienced sustained 99th percentile latency spikes on the Redwood hosted inference path that impacted our checkout recommendation flow. Our telemetry shows a token-level tail latency increase from ~120ms to ~1.4s for ~18% of requests; the checkout retry rate and abandoned-cart metric moved noticeably.

We appreciate the incident postmortem, but our finance and ops teams are requesting an ex-gratia top-up and a 30-day trial extension for the customers who were part of our controlled pilot (approx 1.2M tokens consumed in the window). Can you outline what remediation options you can authorize quickly? We need a succinct proposal to present to our CFO and Legal.

I've attached our internal incident timeline and a quick billing impact export.

— Asha
Asha Menon
Head of Platform Operations, StreamCart

(650) 555-0198

Folks — reviewed the incident timeline and the billing worksheet. Quick summary of my recommendation:

- Incident window: ~2h10m on 2027-03-27.
- Impacted billed tokens during window: ~1,200,000 tokens (per their export).
- Proposed ex-gratia top-up: 1,200,000 tokens (one-to-one makewhole), converted to the equivalent prepaid token credit in their account.
- Additional goodwill: 30-day trial extension for the pilot account (to run high-volume checkout traffic while we validate the runtime fixes).
- Rationale: StreamCart is in an active pilot with potential expansion; the token-top-up keeps the relationship moving without setting a precedent for SLA refunds.

Operational asks if approved:
1) Bill ops to apply a one-time token grant ledger entry (structure provided below).
2) Legal to sign a short ex-gratia acknowledgement (they typically accept a one-page doc).
3) CS to coordinate the trial extension and monitoring hooks (we'll provision a dedicated trace).

If Aditya signs off on the value, I'll prepare the approval form for Marcus to send to StreamCart (DocuSign link + billing ledger entry).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success - Strategic Accounts
monica.patel@redwood.com

Monica / Marcus — reviewed. Approve the one-to-one token top-up of 1,200,000 tokens and the 30-day pilot extension. Please proceed with the following constraints:

- Ex-gratia applied as a one-time prepaid token grant tied to the StreamCart account (not refundable, not transferable).
- Trial extension limited to the pilot environment we have flagged (account tag: streamcart-pilot).
- Legal to sign the acknowledgement doc; streamline the DocuSign to a single signature from StreamCart.
- Finance: cap the internal cost impact to $0. From a GAAP perspective treat as marketing/relationship expense; Monica will coordinate with finance for ledger coding.

Marcus — can you send the approval package (DocuSign envelope + billing action) to Asha and Brian and loop Legal if they want to sign? Once signed, operations should apply the ledger entry and notify CS to enable the pilot extension.

—Aditya

I attached the approval form and the billing worksheet we used (for your review). Let me know if Legal wants any language edits — we kept the acknowledgement deliberately short and non-precedential.

Thanks again — we value the partnership and want to make sure StreamCart can complete the pilot without the thorn of this incident.
